title: British and Irish players in La Liga
brief: Name players from England, Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland or the Republic of Ireland who played in La Liga between 2000/01 and 2025/26.

notes.Ademola Lookman: Ademola Lookman was born in London but plays for Nigeria, so he doesn't count.
notes.Ben Brereton Diaz: Ben Brereton Diaz was born in England but plays for Chile, so he doesn't count.
notes.Yunus Musah: Yunus Musah grew up in England but plays for the United States, so he doesn't count.
notes.Grady Diangana: Grady Diangana grew up in England but plays for DR Congo, so he doesn't count.
notes.Mateo Joseph: Mateo Joseph was born in England but has played for Spain's youth teams, so he doesn't count.
notes.Mohamed-Ali Cho: Mohamed-Ali Cho grew up partly in England but plays for France, so he doesn't count.
notes.Tiago Ilori: Tiago Ilori was born in London but played for Portugal, so he doesn't count.
notes.Jon Toral: Jon Toral was born in Spain and played for Spain's youth teams, so he doesn't count.
notes.Jack Harper: Jack Harper was at Malaga but Transfermarkt shows no La Liga game for him.
notes.Charlie Patino: Charlie Patino has played in Spain, but not in La Liga up to 2025/26.

sources: https://www.transfermarkt.co.uk/ (every La Liga club's league stats page for each season 2000/01 to 2025/26, ES1)
checks: Names are the players listed under England, Northern Ireland, Republic of Ireland, Scotland and Wales in Wikipedia's list of foreign La Liga players with any season from 2000/01 to 2025/26 (30 players; nobody from Northern Ireland). Transfermarkt's league stats pages for all 520 club seasons from 2000/01 to 2025/26 were scanned for every player with a British or Irish citizenship and at least one La Liga appearance: all 30 are there with appearances in the right club and season, and every other player Transfermarkt shows with British or Irish first citizenship is already on the list. Transfermarkt also shows players with a British or Irish second citizenship who represent other countries (Lookman, Brereton Diaz, Musah, Diangana, Cho, Ilori, Mateo Joseph, Jon Toral, Brandon Thomas, Mat Ryan, Wanchope, Yaya Toure); they are left out, as Wikipedia lists them under their national team. Examples are ten of the best known.
